purpose: The smallest source-traceable v1 corpus needed to design and validate intentional v2 migration without preserving accidental implementation behavior.

sourceClassifications.repository_contract_fixture: A checked-in v1 adapter or transport fixture that already defined a provider-facing response boundary.
sourceClassifications.repository_behavior_scenario: A compact JSON rendering of behavior covered by an existing v1 test or implementation path.
sourceClassifications.sanitized_live_shape: A bounded, credential-free rendering of a provider shape recorded by a v1 test as live-observed, with volatile values replaced.

fixtures.neededFor: Keep only the narrow v1 public semantics required to validate v2 exports, machine-readable CLI behavior, library/MCP outcomes, and the explicitly trusted custom-provider protocol.
normalization: No generated bundle paths or internal class names are retained.
CLI and error wording is represented semantically rather than verbatim.

compatibilityExclusions.reason: Meaning, JSON parseability, stream separation, and exit behavior are retained; exact human wording and formatting are not.
Provider, workflow, group, and MCP tool rosters evolve and are validated by version-specific feature tests rather than this compatibility corpus.
Adapter classes, module layout, private types, and implementation inheritance are not public interchange semantics.
Compiled files, declarations, SEA assets, and bundle layouts are rebuilt and validated separately from source-level compatibility.
V1 execution overlap between async and mixed is not retained; mixed migrates to async with notice and v2 async remains durable-only.
benchmark/fixtures/v1 and evaluation datasets measure quality and performance; they are not compatibility inputs.
No synthetic v1 history is created for grok-x-only, grok-combined, or any other provider introduced after v1.
Exact provider IDs, task IDs, paths, timestamps, durations, and request-specific error identifiers are normalized and not contract.
Only primary, replacement, recovery, partial, and exhaustion outcomes are retained; v1 single-level scheduling and ordering are not frozen.
